Purpose 
The Create / Search Application stage is the entry point of the GRO Micro Sales (GMSS) loan journey. It identifies the 
applicant using the applicant's Phone Number and PAN and checks whether an existing application is available to 
continue.

Here is the detailed breakdown of the entity codes P, C, F, and T, followed by two additional common entity types (H 
and A). 
1. 'P' – Person (Individual) 
• Target Entity: Individual human beings. 
• Scope: This is by far the most common PAN type. It applies to salaried individuals, regular citizens, 
professionals, and foreign citizens paying taxes in India. Notably, sole proprietorships do not get a separate 
business PAN; the business taxes are filed under the proprietor's personal 'P' PAN. 
5th Character Rule: For 'P' category PANs, the 5th character will always be the first letter of the individual's surname 
(last name).

• Target Entity: Registered Corporate Entities.

2. 'C' – Company 
• Target Entity: Registered Corporate Entities.
• Scope: This applies to all corporate bodies registered under the Companies Act. It includes Private Limited 
Companies (Pvt Ltd), Public Limited Companies (Ltd), One Person Companies (OPC), Section 8 companies 
(NGOs registered as companies), and foreign companies generating taxable income in India. 
 
• 5th Character Rule: The 5th character represents the first letter of the registered company's name. 
 
3. 'F' – Firm (Partnership) 
• Target Entity: Partnership Firms. 
Scope: This category covers traditional Partnership Firms governed by the Indian Partnership Act of 1932, as well as 
Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) registered under the LLP Act of 2008. Unlike a sole proprietorship, the tax 
department treats a partnership or LLP as a distinct legal entity separate from its individual partners. 
 
• 5th Character Rule: The 5th character represents the first letter of the Firm or LLP's registered name.

4. 'T' – Trust 
• Target Entity: Trusts. 
 
• Scope: Applies to entities legally structured as trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882. This includes 
charitable trusts, private family trusts, religious trusts, and educational trusts holding property or generating 
income for a specific beneficiary or cause. 
 
• 5th Character Rule: The 5th character represents the first letter of the Trust's name.

6. 'A' – Association of Persons (AOP) 
• Target Entity: Association of Persons. 
 
• Scope: An AOP is formed when two or more persons (which can be individuals, companies, or firms) 
voluntarily join together for a common purpose or enterprise to earn income, but do not legally incorporate as 
a company or register as a partnership firm. 
 
• 5th Character Rule: The 5th character represents the first letter of the Association's name. 
 
Note on Remaining Codes: The other entity codes are B (Body of Individuals), G (Government Agency), L (Local 
Authority), and J (Artificial Juridical Person). For all of these non-individual entities, the 5th character is always the 
first letter of the entity's registered name.

The Initial Money Deposit (IMD) stage is the payment stage after the applicable Soft Approval
stage in the UGRO loan application journey. The applicant is required to pay an applicable
initial or login fee before the application can proceed to the next applicable stage. The IMD
amount is calculated internally by the system and is application-specific. The Business
Development Executive (BDE), Sales Agent, or Sales Owner handling the application facilitates
the payment.
The Initial Money Deposit (IMD) screen displays the applicable fee, base amount, tax
components, and total payable amount. The Business Development Executive (BDE) or sales
user receives the payment link through the applicable registered or UGRO email channel and
opens the payment gateway. The observed payment gateway is Easebuzz. The payment
methods shown in the workflow include Debit Card, UPI, Net Banking, and Wallets. Payment
authentication may involve OTP.
